subject: Career
title: Authenticity vs. Curation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Authenticity vs. Curation.

hook.text: 'Be authentic!' But your unfiltered self at 2 AM isn't what LinkedIn followers need.

buildup.text: Personal branding requires curation — choosing what to share, not fabricating who you are.

discovery.text: Erving Goffman's 'impression management' theory says everyone performs different selves in different contexts.

twist.text: The backlash against 'curated' content forgets: every professional interaction is already curated.

climax.text: Authentic branding means consistent values across contexts, not sharing everything everywhere.

punchline.text: Authentic doesn't mean unfiltered. It means consistent.

quiz.question: What did Erving Goffman's theory say about self-presentation?
options: Everyone performs different selves in different contexts
People are always their true selves

details.summary: The tension between authenticity and curation defines modern personal branding. Pure authenticity risks oversharing, while excessive curation creates an unapproachable veneer. The most effective brands balance genuine personality with strategic framing.
details.whyItMatters: Audiences detect inauthenticity quickly, but they also do not want unfiltered streams of consciousness. Finding the balance point builds trust while maintaining professionalism.
takeaways: Share real experiences and opinions but within professional boundaries
Curate for relevance and value rather than for perfection
Vulnerability about professional challenges builds deeper connection

faq.question: How much vulnerability is appropriate in professional personal branding?
faq.answer: Share challenges that you have processed and learned from, not ones you are currently struggling with. Vulnerability about past failures builds connection and credibility. Real-time vulnerability in professional contexts can create discomfort and uncertainty.

faq.question: How do you know if your personal brand is too curated?
faq.answer: If people describe you as polished but hard to relate to, or if your online presence looks significantly different from your day-to-day personality, your curation has gone too far. A trustworthy brand feels consistent between digital and in-person interactions.
